title: “navigate to a fragment” on an initial about:blank with a null latest entry fails “Assert: entriesForNavigationAPI is given.”

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

A fragment navigation of an initial `about:blank` document whose latest entry is still null reaches an assertion in [update document for history step application](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#update-document-for-history-step-application) that can’t hold.

Only two algorithms set a document’s [latest entry](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#latest-entry): update document for history step application, and the [URL and history update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#url-and-history-update-steps). An initial `about:blank` gets one only once something runs the latter on it — as the [window open steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/window-object.html#window-open-steps) (step 4) and the [shared attribute processing steps for iframe and frame elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#shared-attribute-processing-steps-for-iframe-and-frame-elements) (step 4) do, but only when they’re given an `about:blank` URL. So these initial `about:blank` documents have a null latest entry:

- an iframe’s, when its `src` is some other URL that’s still loading;
- a popup’s, when `window.open()` is given some other URL that’s still loading;
- the one a [fresh top-level traversable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#create-a-fresh-top-level-traversable) starts with, since that algorithm navigates straight to *initialNavigationURL*.

A fragment navigation of any of them fails an assertion — e.g. a user opening a link to `about:blank#foo` in a new tab, or a page running this:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<body>
<script>
  const iframe = document.createElement("iframe");
  iframe.src = "/a-page-that-takes-a-while-to-load";
  document.body.append(iframe);
  iframe.contentWindow.location.hash = "foo";
</script>
```

It goes through [navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate) step 15 (*url* equals the active session history entry’s URL `about:blank` with *exclude fragments* set to true, and its fragment is non-null) to [navigate to a fragment](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#navigate-fragid), whose step 15 runs update document for history step application without *entriesForNavigationAPI*. There:

> 1. Let *documentIsNew* be true if *document*'s latest entry is null; otherwise false.

So *documentIsNew* is true, and step 6.5 is taken:

> 5. Otherwise:
>     1. Assert: *entriesForNavigationAPI* is given.

That assertion fails.

And Ladybird conforms to the spec requirements as currently written — including implementing that assertion — so the iframe case above crashed the page’s process in Ladybird.

Other engines don’t have that problem because they don’t conform to the spec requirements: Blink ([`DocumentLoader::CommitSameDocumentNavigationInternal()`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/document_loader.cc)), WebKit ([`FrameLoader::loadInSameDocument()`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/loader/FrameLoader.cpp)), and Gecko ([`nsDocShell::HandleSameDocumentNavigation()`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/docshell/base/nsDocShell.cpp)) all run it as an ordinary same-document navigation.

Chrome fires `popstate` and `hashchange` at the iframe’s window in the example above, and `navigation.currentEntry` stays null — since an initial `about:blank` has [entries and events disabled](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#has-entries-and-events-disabled), so the navigation API’s update is a no-op in all three.

Imaginable ways to fix it:

1. In _“navigate to a fragment”_, before step 15: If the active document’s latest entry is null, set it to the navigable’s active session history entry from before step 14 — the entry the document is displayed by, which is what the URL and history update steps would have given it.
2. Give every initial `about:blank` its initial session history entry as its latest entry when it’s created. That changes what *documentIsNew* means for any later history step application to that document, though — so it reaches further than (1).
